kpis.name: Net Commissions

kpis.name: Capital Ratio

kpis.name: Dividend per Share

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.

kpis.name: Digital Sales

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio calculation (DPS / EPS).

risks.title: Concentrated Geopolitical Exposure in Spain-Mexico-Turkey
risks.summary: BBVA concentrates ~85% of its assets across three markets (Spain, Mexico, Turkey) exposed to distinct political, economic, and sovereign shocks. Rising U.S. tariffs, tensions in Latin America, and institutional instability in Turkey amplify this geographic concentration risk.
risks.score_rationale: Risk ranked first in Item 3D with precise figures (53.1% / 21.2% / 10.6% of assets). Strong language: 'material adverse effect', 'exceptionally high uncertainty'. Upward trend linked to U.S.-China tensions, Ukraine, Middle East, and Latin America.

risks.title: Increasing Multi-Jurisdictional Regulatory and Tax Risk
risks.summary: BBVA must comply simultaneously with European (CRR/CRD), Mexican, and Turkish prudential regimes, with rising capital, liquidity, and consumer protection requirements. The multiplication of sectoral taxes (especially in Spain) and interest rate/fee caps in emerging markets directly weighs on profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned among key business risks: 'increasing tax burden', 'capital, resolution, liquidity, provision and consumer protection requirements'. Present in multiple sections of the filing. Upward trend with new ESG and prudential requirements.

risks.title: Neobank Competition and Technological Obsolescence
risks.summary: The rise of 100% digital neobanks intensifies competitive pressure in BBVA's core markets, particularly in Spain and Mexico. BBVA must simultaneously modernize legacy systems, adopt cloud, AI, and crypto-assets, or risk losing market share in retail and SME segments.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited: 'rise of neobanks (a new generation of financial institutions that operate exclusively online)' and 'ability to manage information technology obsolescence'. Positioned in strategic business risk section. Upward trend with accelerating digitalization.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and Information System Failures
risks.summary: BBVA operates critical IT infrastructure in several high cyber-risk countries. A successful cyberattack or failure of outsourced systems could lead to operational losses, customer data breaches, and regulatory sanctions, with major reputational impact across the group.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned: 'security breaches, including cyber-attacks and identity theft' and 'weaknesses or failures in the Group's internal or outsourced processes, systems (including information technology systems)'. Dedicated Item 16K on cybersecurity confirms its importance. Structurally rising risk in the banking sector.

risks.title: Acquisition and Integration Strategy Risks
risks.summary: BBVA conducts significant external growth operations (including the attempted acquisition of Banco Sabadell in Spain). Failed integrations, cost overruns, or regulatory hurdles related to these transactions could destroy value and divert managerial resources from core operations.
risks.score_rationale: Directly cited: 'the success of our acquisitions and investments, divestitures, mergers, joint ventures and strategic alliances'. 2025 context marked by active M&A (ongoing Sabadell acquisition). Moderate language but concrete execution risk.

risks.title: ESG, Climate, and Institutional Reputation Risks
risks.summary: BBVA faces climate transition risks in its lending portfolios (energy, real estate, industry) and must meet growing ESG commitments imposed by European regulation (CSRD, green taxonomy). Failure to meet these standards or achieve declared targets exposes the group to reputational and legal risks.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned: 'physical, regulatory, reputational, transition and business risks associated with climate change and emerging and developing ESG standards'. Presence in emerging markets assessed at 'higher ESG risk levels'. Strong upward trend in European regulatory pressure.

risks.title: AML, Anti-Corruption, and Sanctions Compliance Risks
risks.summary: BBVA's presence in high AML/CTF risk markets (Mexico, Turkey, Latin America) exposes the group to compliance failures that could result in massive regulatory fines, operational restrictions, or criminal proceedings, as illustrated by recent sector precedents in international banking.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited: 'weaknesses or failures of our anti-money laundering or anti-terrorism programs' and 'compliance with applicable anti-corruption laws and sanctions regulations'. Operations in high AML-risk emerging markets (Mexico, Turkey). Strong language on potential consequences.

risks.title: Hyperinflationary Environment in Turkey and Argentina
risks.summary: Turkish and Argentine economies are classified as hyperinflationary (IAS 29), requiring BBVA to restate Garanti BBVA's entire financial statements at closing exchange rates. The liraization strategy imposed by Turkish authorities compresses margins and limits Garanti BBVA's balance sheet management freedom, which represents ~10.6% of group assets.
risks.score_rationale: Detailed in financial presentation section with application of IAS 29 since 2022 (Turkey) and 2018 (Argentina). 'Liraization strategy' and negative real rates in Turkey cited as specific risks affecting margins. Stable but structurally constraining trend.

ai_positioning.summary: BBVA is gradually integrating AI into its customer services and operations, without positioning as a technology leader. Focus is on incremental innovation.
